transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korva Coleman.
Ukraine's Air Force says it received no intelligence from allies
on Russian ballistic missiles that have hit Ukrainian cities over the last two days.
The country's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, spoke to NPR's Joanna Kokissis in Kiev.
Zelensky told NPR on Tuesday that five ballistic missiles hit the Kiev region the previous night.
And we didn't get the information about ballistic missiles.
This is really our weak place.
He said his military was told it was due to a technical glitch, not to anyone withholding information.
The Trump administration paused intelligence sharing with Ukraine in early 2025,
so Ukraine diversified its sources.
We get from the United States very necessary information, but not only from the United States.
Zelensky confirmed to NPR that the White House is again threatening to cut off this information
because of Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries.
Joanna Kokissis, NPR News, Kiev.
In the U.S., federal regulators are fining Bank of America more than a billion dollars.
That is for failing to prevent money laundering by its customers.
According to American bear, Scott Horsley reports this marks one of the largest penalties on record by the Treasury Department.
Banks are required to track and report financial transactions they suspect may be tied to illegal activity.
The Treasury Department says B of A willfully ignored that requirement
and allowed more than five billion dollars' worth of money to change hands without proper reporting
over a seven-year period stretching back to 2018.
Some of the suspicious moves showed signs of Chinese money laundering networks.
Others had apparent ties to the southwest border.
The bank also agreed to pay more than 11 million dollars to settle apparent sanctions violations
involving Iran, Russia and other targets.
The bank says in a statement it's committed billions of dollars and thousands of employees
to improving its financial compliance.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The family of a man killed by a tiger at a zoo in northern England
is appealing to the public not to share video of the attack on social media.
President Trump is among those who've shared it, as NPR's Lauren Frayer reports from London.
William Chapman's family says he suffered from significant mental illness.
Last weekend, the 23-year-old climbed over safety barriers into a tiger enclosure
and witnesses recorded his final moments as a tiger mauled him.
President Trump is among those who've shared the video, adding a caption,
"Don't ever mess with nature, President D.J.T."
Later, he posted an AI-generated video of himself in a similar stance as Chapman,
but taming the tiger.
Without singling out Trump, Chapman's family calls such posts deeply offensive
at an exceptionally vulnerable time for them
and is asking the public to stop sharing the video.
Lauren Frayer, NPR News, London.
You're listening to NPR News.
The government will release its latest report on consumer prices later this morning.
Economists are watching to see how rising energy prices affect consumers' pocketbooks.
President Trump has spent the night in Las Vegas.
Later today, he'll travel a little bit south to Bullhead City, Arizona for another campaign rally.
This evening, he goes to Kalispell, Montana for another political event.
NASA's mechanical rover on Mars, the Perseverance, has just logged a major milestone.
The space agency says it completed the longest total drive distance by a vehicle on another world.
NPR's Ari Daniel has more.
That distance is 28 miles, which may not seem like much by earthly standards,
but project scientist Katie Stack Morgan says it's a big deal for an off-world rover.
This is the culmination of how we explore the solar system
and the capabilities that we bring to other planets.
Over the last half-decade, Perseverance has collected possible evidence of life in Jezero Crater
and sampled rocks that might represent the first half-billion years of solar system history.
It collected material from the Martian surface so that one day, another mission might return those samples to Earth.
But this part of the program has an uncertain future,
given its hefty price tag put it in the crosshairs of the federal government earlier this year.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
Forecasters say Hurricane Simon is moving north in the Pacific.
It's aimed right at the lower tip of Baja, California.
It may lose strength before it makes landfall.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Ukraine's Air Force says it got no allied intelligence on Russian ballistic missiles hitting cities
Bank of America to pay over $1 billion in fines for failing to prevent money laundering
Chapman's family asks public not to share video of tiger attack at northern England zoo
Trump shares tiger attack video and posts AI video of himself taming the tiger
Government to release latest consumer price report, with energy prices in focus
President Trump in Las Vegas, with rallies planned in Arizona and Montana
NASA's Perseverance rover sets record for longest total drive distance on another world
Forecasters track Hurricane Simon moving north toward the tip of Baja California
